verdict.rationale: Shortwave's Splits feature divides one inbox into multiple focused inboxes, each in its own tab. Splits can be defined by Importance, built-in or custom labels, specific senders, or complex search queries, and auto-apply rules can label mail automatically to drive a Split. The docs frame this as handling different email types at different times so you stay responsive where it matters most, which matches priority-order triage. Missing for 10: no explicit documentation of newsletter or calendar-invite Splits as named presets, and no independent hands-on corroboration of Splits specifically (community praise covers Bundles grouping, not Splits).

support.subject: As a power-user, I can split my inbox into focused streams — important, team, newsletters, calendar invites — so triage happens in priority order, not arrival order

citations.quote: They’re a simple way to divide your one big inbox into multiple smaller, more focused inboxes – each in its own tab.
You can define Splits based on: Importance, Built-in labels... Custom labels, Specific senders, Complex search queries
Splits let you handle different types of emails at different times, so you can stay responsive where it matters most.
For even more power, you can use Gmail filters or Shortwave’s auto-apply rules to apply a label automatically to emails, and then create a Split based on that label.
